smell: github.com/charmbracelet/ultraviolet v0.0.0-20260416155717-489999b90468 is pinned to a pseudo-version (commit SHA, not a tagged release). The version string encodes a commit hash — but the project has never tagged a release, so this is de-facto HEAD tracking of an unreleased library. The same project is pulled by four different charm.land deps at three different pseudo-versions (bubbles uses 20260205, lipgloss+log use 20251205, bubbletea + main require use 20260416). MVS picks the newest. This is how the charm ecosystem works today — but the exposure is: no stable-API contract, zero release notes, zero changelog between bumps.
fix_summary: Acceptance note. Charm ecosystem convention is that ultraviolet (the internal renderer) is not publicly-tagged. Treat every charm.land/* bump as an implicit ultraviolet bump and test the wizard end-to-end (internal/tui/wizard/** is already excluded from most audits — this is precisely why). No action on the pin itself; document the convention and schedule quarterly 'bump charm.land libs' in roadmap.md so drift is visible.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: charm libs intentional UI stack

smell: golang.org/x/exp pinned at v0.0.0-20231006140011 (Oct 2023) — almost 2.5 years old. Pulled transitively by charm.land/log/v2, which only imports golang.org/x/exp/slog (a BACKPORT of log/slog that the stdlib now provides since Go 1.21 — and this repo targets 1.25 per go.mod). charm.land/log/v2's go.mod still requires x/exp for the slog path. Go 1.25 makes x/exp/slog entirely redundant for us — but we can't fix it; charm.land/log/v2 requires the old pin.
fix_summary: File upstream issue at github.com/charmbracelet/log requesting a drop of the x/exp/slog import in favor of stdlib log/slog. Until that lands, the stale pin persists. Alternative: add an explicit 'require golang.org/x/exp <newer>' in our go.mod to force a bump — but this is fighting MVS for no real gain since we don't directly import x/exp. Seam #10: modernization owns the 'drop x/exp in favor of stdlib' fix, but the fix sits in a DEPENDENCY not our code — so it's truly neither skill's action.

smell: goreleaser-action is SHA-pinned (good), but the version parameter it resolves IS a tag, not a SHA — version: v2.15.2 in both release.yml and release-prep.yml. This is the goreleaser CLI binary version, not the GH Action. The action downloads the goreleaser CLI from GitHub releases at runtime. If goreleaser releases were ever re-tagged (a malicious force-push to a tag), we'd pull a different binary. Acceptable trade-off because (a) goreleaser is a widely-used project, (b) its releases are cosigned, but worth noting.

  with:
    version: "v2.15.2"
fix_summary: Minor tightening: if goreleaser publishes binary SHA256s (it does, as part of its own release process), add a post-install `sha256sum goreleaser` step and match against a pinned hash. Alternatively, accept the v2.15.2 tag trust model — goreleaser signs its own releases with cosign. No urgent action.

smell: goreleaser sboms stanza scopes `artifacts: archive` — only the tar.gz archive gets a CycloneDX SBOM. The nfpms stanza emits .deb and .rpm packages (line 62-76) that also land on the release, but no SBOM is produced for them. Users who install via `apt`/`dnf` from the published .deb/.rpm therefore get no machine-readable dependency manifest, even though the same binary is inside. Supply-chain transparency regression relative to the tar.gz path.
evidence:
// .goreleaser.yaml:39-45
sboms:
  - id: default
    artifacts: archive          # ← only tar.gz
    documents:
      - "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}.sbom.json"
    cmd: syft
    args: ["$artifact", "--output", "cyclonedx-json=$document"]
// .goreleaser.yaml:62-76 — nfpms deb/rpm with no corresponding sbom id
fix_summary:
Add a second sboms entry scoped to `artifacts: package` (goreleaser's nfpm artifact class) so .deb and .rpm get sibling .sbom.json files. Example:

```yaml
sboms:
  - id: archive
    artifacts: archive
    documents:
      - "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}.sbom.json"
    cmd: syft
    args: ["$artifact", "--output", "cyclonedx-json=$document"]
  - id: package
    artifacts: package
    documents:
      - "{{ .ArtifactName }}.sbom.json"
    cmd: syft
    args: ["$artifact", "--output", "cyclonedx-json=$document"]
```

Effect: apt/dnf users get parity with tar.gz users on supply-chain visibility. Release.yml already runs sbom-action/download-syft so the binary is available.
